report.tagline: A global app where people book homes, rooms, experiences and services from local hosts instead of hotels.
report.simpleSummary: Airbnb lets ordinary people rent out their flat, spare room or holiday home to travellers. As a guest, you search a city, see photos, reviews and the total price, and book in the app. Since 2025 you can also book local experiences, like a cooking class, and services, like a private chef or massage, often from the same hosts. Airbnb keeps a fee on every booking and does not own any of the homes.

overview.whatItDoes: Airbnb is a two-sided marketplace: hosts list places to stay, experiences and services, and guests book them. Airbnb handles search, payments, reviews, messaging and support. Since the May 2025 relaunch it is trying to become a full travel app, adding services, experiences, hotels and car rentals.
howItWorks: Hosts create a listing with photos, a calendar and a price, and set house rules and a cancellation policy.
Guests search by place and dates, see the total price including fees, and book instantly or send a request.
Airbnb takes payment and pays the host about 24 hours after check-in, minus a host fee of about 15.5%.
After the stay, guest and host review each other, which builds trust for the next booking.
AirCover protects guests against bad listings and hosts against damage, and AI support now solves about 40% of issues without a person.
overview.valueProposition: For guests: more space, a kitchen and a local feel, often cheaper than hotels for groups and families. For hosts: extra income from a home they already own, with Airbnb handling payments and trust.

businessModel.summary: Airbnb earns a fee on every booking. Most hosts now pay a single fee of about 15.5% of the booking value, and guests see one total price. Airbnb is adding ads and new categories to earn more per trip.

revenueStreams.detail: About 15.5% host-only fee on most bookings. The bulk of revenue.
A cut of each class, tour, chef or massage booked.
Commissions on hotel nights and CarTrawler car rentals.
Airbnb holds guest money before paying hosts and earns interest on it.
Paid visibility for hosts being built into the AI agent.

businessModel.pricing: Free to list and search. Most hosts pay about 15.5% of each booking. A direct booking link pilot cuts this to 6% or 10%. Guests see a total price including any fees.
costDrivers: Legal and compliance costs for city rules
businessModel.unitEconomics: Rough example. A guest books 3 nights at $179 a night, so about $537. The host pays about 15.5%, so Airbnb keeps about $83. Payment fees take maybe $12, support and AirCover a few dollars, and marketing for that booking perhaps $10 to $15, since most guests come direct or through free search. That leaves Airbnb roughly $50 before staff and tech. This is why Airbnb is very profitable: it has no buildings, and most guests find it without paid ads.

howTheyGetUsers: Direct traffic and app opens, as most guests type 'Airbnb' themselves
Brand ads and free search results

Host referrals and 'Airbnb your home' campaigns

whatBringsUsersBack: Good past stays build trust in the brand
Reviews make guests careful and hosts keen to keep high ratings
Experiences and services give reasons to open the app beyond stays
growth.moat: Airbnb has millions of unique homes that are not on hotel sites, and years of reviews on both hosts and guests. More hosts bring more guests, which brings more hosts: a strong network effect. Its brand is also a verb, so many guests skip Google and come straight to the app, which keeps marketing costs low.

improvementIdeas.idea: Verified listing check: Airbnb confirms photos and key amenities for top-searched homes
improvementIdeas.problem: Guests complain listings do not match photos.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer refunds and higher review scores.

improvementIdeas.idea: Cap checkout chores and show them before booking
improvementIdeas.problem: Guests resent paying cleaning fees and still being asked to clean.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Mentions of chores in negative reviews

improvementIdeas.idea: Let hosts opt out of Pay Later with a lower fee trade-off
improvementIdeas.problem: Hosts lose bookings to late cancellations under Pay Later.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Lower host churn while keeping most Pay Later growth.

improvementIdeas.idea: Bundle a service suggestion at checkout for each stay
improvementIdeas.problem: Services and experiences are hard to discover.

improvementIdeas.idea: Guaranteed rebooking within 1 hour if a host cancels inside 7 days
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Higher guest trust and repeat bookings.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Repeat rate of guests who faced a host cancellation

pmLessons: Trust is the real product in a marketplace of strangers: reviews, protection and support make it possible.
Changing fees moves money between hosts and guests. Every pricing change needs a plan for the side that loses.
Growth features like Pay Later can raise bookings and cancellations at the same time, so watch both.
Expanding into new categories works best when it uses an existing habit, like adding services to a stay.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow Airbnb Services in a city like Mumbai?
interviewQuestions.hint: Start with which services travellers want, recruit supply, place offers in the stay journey, measure attach rate and repeat bookings.

interviewQuestions.question: Cancellations rose from 16% to 19% after Pay Later. Is that a problem?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare net nights booked against host harm and empty dates. Segment by policy and trip type. Suggest fixes and guardrails.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Airbnb's north star, and how would you break it down?
interviewQuestions.hint: Nights and seats booked, split into supply, demand, conversion and completed trips, each with team-level metrics.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you handle a city banning most short-term rentals?
interviewQuestions.hint: Think about hosts, guests and the city. Options: compliance tools, longer stays, hotels in that city. Measure lost nights and recovery.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature to reduce guest disappointment at arrival.
interviewQuestions.hint: Find the main gaps (photos, cleanliness, check-in), choose one, propose verification or checklists, measure complaints and ratings.
